routes.description: Establish a cumulative inference from cosmic origins, physical and biological order, objective moral obligation, and immaterial features of human life to a personal creator, then explain the evidential bridge from generic theism to Christian claims.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the combined explanatory case warrants a personal, intelligent, and moral creator; survives naturalistic and anti-theist objections; and supplies a distinct evidential basis for moving from generic theism to Christianity.

motionBridge.description: Show that the cumulative evidence makes Christian theism a better account of the motion's principal domains than atheistic materialism and the anti-theist alternative.

centralBridges.description: Connect the universe's beginning and contingent existence to a supernatural personal cause while answering objections from ignorance, natural explanation, and cosmic destruction.
Connect fine-tuning and biological information to intelligent agency while addressing evolutionary explanation, underdetermination, apparent defects, suffering, and extinction.
Distinguish moral knowledge and conduct from the ontological grounding of objective obligation, then identify a transcendent moral source.
Provide an evidential route from possible divine action to resurrection and Christian authority without treating generic design or cosmic origins alone as proof of Christianity.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain consciousness, rational thought, mathematics, and freedom as realities whose grounding bears on the comparison between theism and materialism.
Separate the existence question from religious wrongdoing and distinguish evidence for a creator from unsupported selection among particular deities.

routes.description: Reject the claimed inferences from unexplained or complex features of reality to a supervising deity, contest the move from a possible designer to Christianity, and establish the independent moral and political case against divine authority and organized religion.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the pro evidence does not warrant its theistic and Christian conclusions, secular accounts remain sufficient without a divine posit, and the doctrines or authority structures under review support the motion-level anti-theist critique.

motionBridge.description: Show both that God's existence has not been warranted by the offered inferences and that the proposed religious authority is morally or socially objectionable.

centralBridges.description: Maintain the claimant's burden for a creator and show why uncertainty, cosmic beginnings, order, or scientific gaps do not by themselves license a personal divine cause.
Test design and providence against natural explanation, biological underdetermination, apparent defects, extinction, suffering, and the delayed history of revelation.
Account for conscience, moral action, and self-sacrifice without divine sanction while challenging reward, punishment, and command as foundations of genuine morality.
Connect doctrines of surveillance, punishment, sacrifice, apocalypse, and claimed divine command to the anti-theist objection concerning autonomy, coercion, and political domination.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Preserve the distinction between a speculative cosmic designer and the intervening God, miracles, resurrection, redemption, and authority claimed by Christianity.
Explain religious belief and supervision in human psychological or institutional terms without treating believers' conviction as mind-independent evidence.

sections.title: Cosmic Origins, Causation, and the Explanatory Burden
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether the universe's beginning warrants a personal supernatural cause or instead leaves an unresolved question on which the theistic claimant retains the burden of proof.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Biological Information, and Providential Design
sections.rationale: This issue joins the physical and biological design inferences with objections from natural explanation, underdetermination, imperfection, suffering, extinction, and the purposes attributed to a designer.

sections.title: Objective Moral Grounding, Conscience, and Secular Virtue
sections.rationale: This issue distinguishes the grounding of objective duties from moral knowledge and behavior, while testing whether conscience, empathy, and self-sacrifice require or are altered by divine authority.

sections.title: Consciousness, Reason, Mathematics, and Human Freedom
sections.rationale: This issue addresses the cumulative argument from immaterial or normative features of human life and asks what explanatory consequences follow for theism and materialism.

sections.title: Christian Claims, Divine Authority, and the Anti-Theist Critique
sections.rationale: This issue tests the bridge from generic theism to miracles, resurrection, redemption, and Christian authority, together with objections concerning punishment, sacrifice, autonomy, coercion, and apocalyptic politics.
